title: Nimble reserve hire-credit curve
content:
Purpose:
Prototype a compact, trigger-driven headcount plan tied to prepaid credit purchases and GPU mix reserves. This sheet translates a small credit buffer (nimble reserve) into hiring cadence and runway adjustments under price-sensitivity shocks. Intended for GTM + Finance alignment and to feed Dedicated capacity commit guidance.

Executive summary (one para):
We model a 12-month horizon where small prepay credit increments are used as a lever to defer 0.5–3.0 FTE hires depending on price movement in per-token cost and GPU spot availability. The core idea: maintain a nimble reserve (3–6 weeks of burst credit) that can be spent preferentially on high-margin features to avoid immediate hiring, then use trigger rules to convert credit consumption into hiring or price adjustments. This reduces hiring lumpy costs while keeping SLA-backed throughput.

Key assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline monthly effective unit cost (hosted API per 1M tokens): $120 (baseline).
- GPU pool reserved cost equivalence: 1 reserved GPU-month ~ $14,000 (for Dedicated equivalence).
- Nimble reserve target: $250k in credits (~18 days of burst at current run-rate).
- Average monthly token demand growth: +9% mo/mo.
- Average engineer SDE-II fully burdened cost: $26k/month.
- Hiring lag (requisition to fully productive): 10 weeks.
- Credit conversion efficiency: each $50k credit offsets ~0.2 FTE of immediate capacity (through burst + higher model quantization).

Interpretation of columns:
- starting-credits: dollar value of prepaid credits at month start.
- net-credit-purchases: incremental prepay buys planned that month.
- credit-spend: credits used to absorb burst and model costs.
- demand-index: relative token demand vs Jan baseline.
- price-shock-adjusted-cost: baseline unit cost * (1 + price-movement) where price movement is a function of model mix + GPU spot compression.
- implied-deferred-hires: (credit-spend / 50k) * 0.2 FTE-equivalence — a heuristic to show how much hiring we avoided that month.

Scenario definitions (3):
- Base (above): moderate credit buys in Feb, Jun, Dec to smooth purchases and maintain a 3–6 week buffer.
- Credit-rich: aggressive prepay in Feb/Jun/Oct (adds +$150k each) enabling deferral of >3 FTE over the year if unit price holds.
- Price-shock: sustained +30% unit cost beginning Mar (maps to price_shock_adjusted_cost in CSV). Triggers immediate hiring conversion once credits fall below $60k and demand > +15% month-over-month.

Trigger rules (operational):
- If ending-credits < $60k and demand-index increase > +12% MoM => trigger immediate requisition for 0.5 FTE and notify Revenue Ops.
- If cumulative-hires > 1.5 FTE ahead of plan and ending-credits > $200k => pause hires for 4 weeks and re-evaluate model quantization settings.
- If unit cost > baseline * 1.25 for two consecutive months => evaluate price-tier increase for low-margin customers (prep a 15% pass-through).

Financial linkage (how this maps to P&L / Dedicated commit):
- Prepay credits show up as deferred revenue/contra-cost depending on accounting; we model them conservatively as an OPEX buffer.
- Each 1 FTE deferred for 6 months saves ~ $156k in cash-basis comp costs (includes taxes/benefits).
- Buying credits at strategic times (e.g., Jun low spot prices) can yield 8–14% effective cost reduction vs spot-run-rate.

Open questions / caveats:
- The 0.2 FTE per $50k credit conversion factor is a heuristic derived from last year’s burst runs; needs backtest against Q1 actuals.
- Accounting treatment of prepaid credits across regions with different tax regimes (APAC) may alter net benefit.
- Hiring lag variability: if recruiting slows, the deferred-hire benefit compounds differently.

Quick action items (next 6 weeks):
- [Finance] build a small Monte Carlo to test heuristic across demand shocks (owner: Marco, due: 2026-02-26).
- [GTM] prepare a 15% pass-through messaging template for low-margin customers (owner: Leah, due: 2026-03-05).
- [People Ops] validate hiring lag assumptions by role (owner: Ava, due: 2026-02-20).

Notes-to-self / scratch bits:
- Consider tying credit buys to calendar-seasonality (holiday spikes) and to Dedicated commit negotiation windows.
- Could offer customers a new SKU: "nimble-reserve credits" sold in $50k blocks with built-in rollover — impacts both revenue recognition and stickiness.
- TODO: get precise GPU-month equivalent mapping by instance family (A10 vs H100).

Quick sensitivity chart idea (one-liner for deck):
"Every incremental $100k in nimble credits buys ~0.6 FTE months of runway at base price; under a 25% price shock that drops to ~0.31 FTE months — illustrates how credits are a convex hedge but not a complete substitute for capacity hires."

End of sheet.
